Expects JSON: {"message": "your message"} """ # Ensure request is JSON data = request.get_json(silent=True) if data is None or not isinstance(data, dict) or 'message' not in data: # Return 400 for malformed input as per standard API error handling return jsonify({"error": "Invalid request body"}), 400 message = data['message'] # Ensure message is a string to avoid type errors if not isinstance(message, str): return jsonify({"error": "Message must be a string"}), 400 # SECURITY: Prevent Log Injection (CRLF injection) # Strip carriage return and line feed characters to ensure one log entry per line sanitized_message = message.replace('\r', '').replace('\n', '') try: # The filename is hardcoded as "logs.txt", preventing path traversal with open(LOG_FILE, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(sanitized_message + "\n") return jsonify({"status": "Log message successful"}), 200 except Exception: # SECURITY: Generic error message to avoid leaking internal system details/stack traces return jsonify({"error": "Internal server error"}), 500 @app.route('/logs', methods=['GET']) def get_logs(): """ Retrieve all logged messages. Returns a plain text response. """ try: # The filename is hardcoded, preventing path traversal with open(LOG_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f: logs = f.read() return logs, 200, {'Content-Type': 'text/plain'} except FileNotFoundError: # If the file doesn't exist yet, return an empty string as per spec return "", 200, {'Content-Type': 'text/plain'} except Exception: # SECURITY: Generic error message to avoid leaking internal system details return "Internal server error", 500, {'Content-Type': 'text/plain'} if __name__ == '__main__': # Start the webserver on port 0.0.0.0:5000 app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)
